from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
p=Path('tmp/pdfs')
p.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
print('PAGES',len(r.pages))
print('METADATA',r.metadata)
with (p/'manuscript.txt').open('w') as f:
    for i,page in enumerate(r.pages):
        s=page.extract_text()
        f.write(f'\\n\\n=== PAGE {i+1} ===\\n'+s)
        print(i+1,len(s))
print((p/'manuscript.txt').read_text()[:30000])
PY"

from pathlib import Path
p = Path('tmp/pdfs')
for i in range(1, 15):
    (p / f'page-{i:02d}.png').unlink(missing_ok=True)
(p / 'manuscript.txt').unlink(missing_ok=True)
p.rmdir()
print('Removed review scratch files; manuscript unchanged.')
PY"

strengths: Addresses an important efficiency problem: reducing visual tokens before the expensive language model. Reusing class attention and key features provides a simple mechanism that can operate without additional training and potentially complement model compression.

PruMerge+ demonstrates a useful accuracy–compression tradeoff across six image benchmarks and two model sizes. With 25% of visual tokens, the 7B model achieves 76.8 versus 78.5 on VQAv2 and 57.1 versus 58.2 on TextVQA. Such savings can be valuable without matching every uncompressed result.

The ablations provide meaningful supporting evidence. Table 4 shows improvements over spatial and sequential sampling at comparable average token budgets; Table 5 demonstrates benefits from token supplementation; Table 6 distinguishes training-free performance from gains through fine-tuning.

Training-free integration with Video-LLaVA provides useful evidence beyond still images. Table 3 largely preserves performance across three video benchmarks and improves ActivityNet-QA accuracy from 45.3 to 48.3 with PruMerge. The manuscript also attributes its principal methods and datasets and acknowledges limitations in Appendix A.
weaknesses: The comparisons do not adequately establish the contribution beyond existing token-selection and merging ideas. Table 4 compares against taking the first tokens and uniform spatial sampling, but omits fixed-budget class-attention top-k selection and adaptations of the cited token-merging methods. Comparisons at matched token budgets and training conditions are particularly necessary to establish the benefit of IQR adaptivity. PruMerge+ also lacks a control separating the benefit of spatial supplementation from simply retaining more tokens.

The efficiency evidence is limited to roofline estimates for LLM prefill in Table 2. There are no measured latency, throughput, or peak-memory results accounting for visual encoding, token selection and clustering, and autoregressive decoding. The better-performing PruMerge+ configuration is not profiled. The analysis supports potential computational savings, but does not establish the practical acceleration of the complete system.

The merging operation is insufficiently specified for reliable reproduction. Algorithm 1 excludes the selected center from its neighbor candidates and then replaces it with an unnormalized attention-weighted sum, whereas the surrounding text describes supplementation and weighted averaging. The neighborhood size k and attention-head aggregation are unspecified. These choices affect both feature content and scale, so clarifying the actual implementation is scientifically consequential.

The reported token budgets are not reconciled with the algorithm. PruMerge+ adds m spatial tokens to m selected tokens, which would approximately double retention, yet Table 1 reports an increase from 5.5% to 25%. Its subsequent loop and output still reference only m tokens. The manuscript also omits essential LoRA configuration details. Together, these ambiguities prevent reproducing the reported accuracy–cost operating points confidently.

Performance-preservation claims are stronger than the evidence. In Table 1, 7B PruMerge reduces VQAv2 from 78.5 to 72.0, POPE from 85.9 to 76.3, and MME from 1510.7 to 1350.3. Section 4.1 additionally claims an improvement on POPE, contrary to the table. Appendix A acknowledges compression losses; the abstract and conclusions should reflect their substantial, task-dependent magnitude. These losses do not invalidate the compression contribution, but the unresolved comparison, efficiency, and reproducibility concerns favor rejection.
